**What I found:** `src/lib/retry.ts` should move down: delete it and turn on the `retry` option that `got` 14 already has (the record calls this L4 CODE → L3 LIB). The `isEligibleForDiscount` copies should not move down, because your own discount policy has no outside home and `src/shared/discount.ts` would still belong to your team. That deduplication is ordinary refactoring, not bring-down.

**Why it matters:** By default, `got` only retries GET, PUT, HEAD, DELETE, OPTIONS and TRACE, so the default never retries a POST, which is what caused both incidents. Keeping the wrapper means you keep paying for bug fixes (six last quarter) on behavior a maintained, approved package already handles.

**Do this first:**
1. Move one real outbound client to a shared `got.extend({ retry: { limit, methods, statusCodes, backoffLimit } })` instance, leaving `methods` at the default with POST excluded. Remove its call into `src/lib/retry.ts` and check that no request is sent twice.
2. Move the remaining callers, delete `src/lib/retry.ts`, and add an ESLint `no-restricted-imports` ban on that path.
3. Merging the discount copies is your team's call as a refactor, outside this skill.

**What I did not check:** The workspace has no `package.json` or `src/`, so I relied on your description.
- Whether the wrapper retries anything `got`'s settings can't express: `git log -p src/lib/retry.ts`
- The installed `got` version and that the repo runs as ESM (`got` 14 is ESM-only): `npm ls got`
- Whether any caller deliberately retries POSTs, for example with idempotency keys: `grep -rn "retry(" src/`
- Whether the three discount copies are really identical: `diff` the three files

```
Scope:          One Node.js 22 TypeScript API repo, one 4-person team; src/lib/retry.ts and 3 copies of isEligibleForDiscount
Mode:           Assessment
Decision:       Move src/lib/retry.ts L4 CODE -> L3 LIB (got 14 retry option). No bring-down for isEligibleForDiscount; hand off.
Summary:        The hand-written retry is generic commodity behavior and needs ongoing fixes. got 14, already approved and
                already wrapping every call, ships the same behavior with a safer default that leaves POST out of its retry methods.
                The discount function is your own policy, and the proposed new home has the same owner, so it does not count as
                bring-down. Main risk: a caller that depends on wrapper behavior got can't express.

Candidates:
- src/lib/retry.ts
  - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB (distance 1)
  - Landing: got 14 `retry` option (limit, methods, statusCodes, errorCodes, calculateDelay, backoffLimit,
             maxRetryAfter) set once via got.extend(); hooks.beforeRetry for logging and metrics
  - Owners: API team -> got maintainers (sindresorhus/got); approved by the platform team
  - Evidence: 140 LOC; 6 bug-fix commits last quarter; 2 production incidents from retried non-idempotent POSTs;
              got's built-in retry is currently switched off; nothing domain-specific
  - Variation: none reported. If a caller needs a POST retry, it opts in per request with an idempotency key; no blocker
  - Confidence: High (based on your description; code not inspected)
  - Next action: move one client to a got.extend() instance with retry turned on; confirm POST gets no retry and GET/5xx retries

Priorities:
1. src/lib/retry.ts
   - Why now: recent production incidents and high churn; the replacement is already installed and approved
   - Move: L4 CODE -> L3 LIB
   - Landing: got 14 `retry` option on a shared got.extend() instance
   - Migration proof: one real outbound client, with a test showing POST is not retried and GET on 503 is
   - Retire: delete src/lib/retry.ts; ban importing it with ESLint no-restricted-imports

Gaps:
- Code not available in this workspace. Wrapper semantics, the got version, and ESM compatibility are unverified
- Unknown whether the wrapper adds anything got lacks (circuit breaking, a retry budget, jitter policy). If it does,
  that part needs its own landing, not a rewrite

Handoffs:
- isEligibleForDiscount (3 identical copies, 40 LOC each)
  - Reason excluded: your own discount policy (it is what differentiates you, so it stays L4 CODE);
    src/shared/discount.ts would keep the same owner, which makes it a refactor
  - Better skill: functionality-complexity-tradeoff (are all 3 copies still needed?), then
    morphogenetic-architecture (where the module goes in the codebase), then architecture-as-code (stop new copies)
```

No library search was needed: `got` is already installed and on the platform team's approved list.
